cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend: the Philistines are camped at Michmash, and in the whole army of Saul, Israel's king, only Saul and his son Jonathan even have a sword or spear (1 Samuel 13:16, 22). Then one day Jonathan turns to the young man who carries his armor. He says, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.”

cards.question: Before he goes, Jonathan tells his father Saul about the plan.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Saul is staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron, on the outskirts of Gibeah. And his army has been shrinking for a while now (1 Samuel 13:8).

cards.question: Saul's troops with him at Migron number about ___ men.

cards.text: Ahijah is there too, a priest wearing an ephod. He's the great-grandson of Eli, the priest of the LORD in Shiloh.

cards.question: Saul's troops know that Jonathan has left.

cards.text: Now here's what stands between Jonathan and that Philistine outpost: a pass he has to cross to get there.

cards.question: The pass Jonathan plans to cross has ___ on both sides.

cards.text: And these cliffs have NAMES: Bozez and Seneh, one standing to the north toward Michmash and the other to the south toward Geba. Friend, I named six cookie cutters, but it never crossed my mind to name a ROCK.
Jonathan turns to his armor-bearer again: “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men.” Then he says what he's counting on.

cards.question: Two men against a whole Philistine outpost. What does Jonathan say about the LORD?

answers.text: Nothing can stop Him from saving by many or by few
He only saves when the army is big enough
He will fight for them once Saul arrives

cards.text: He starts with “Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf.” PERHAPS, friend, he doesn't know how this ends, but he knows Who can't be stopped.

cards.question: Jonathan just pitched a two-man attack on an outpost. What does his armor-bearer say?

answers.text: Go ahead because I am with you
Let us go back and ask your father
Let us wait until more men come

cards.text: Heart and soul, no questions asked. Friend, that's the guy who says yes to helping you move before you even tell him which floor.
Here's Jonathan's plan: they'll cross over and let the Philistines see them. Whatever the outpost says next tells them what to do.

cards.question: If the Philistines say wait until we come to you, what will Jonathan and his armor-bearer do?
And if the Philistines say come on up, what does Jonathan say that will be?

answers.text: Their sign the LORD has handed them over
Their sign to go back and get Saul
Their sign that the outpost is a trap

cards.text: The two of them step into view, and the Philistines crack that the Hebrews are coming out of the holes they've been hiding in. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for years, and even I felt that one.

cards.question: Moment of truth. What do the men of the outpost call out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer?

answers.text: Come on up and we will teach you a lesson
Wait there until we come down to you
Turn around and go back to your homes

cards.question: Jonathan tells his armor-bearer to follow him, because the LORD has delivered the Philistines into the hand of Israel.

cards.text: So Jonathan climbs up on his hands and feet, his armor-bearer right behind him. Hands AND feet, friend, straight toward the men who just promised to teach them a lesson.

cards.question: Jonathan makes it to the top of the cliff. What happens to the Philistines there?

cards.text: His armor-bearer follows and finishes them off, and it all happens in about half an acre of land. That's not a battlefield, friend, that's a BACKYARD.

cards.question: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer strike down about ___ men.

cards.text: Then panic hits the Philistines everywhere: in the camp, in the field and among all the people. Even the outposts and the raiding parties are trembling.

cards.question: As the panic spreads, even the earth quakes.
Two men started it, but the text says where all that panic came from. The panic spread from ___.

cards.text: Over at Gibeah, Saul's watchmen look across and see the Philistine troops melting away and scattering in every direction. I bet Saul's standing there like somebody who hears the whole office cheering and has NO idea what he missed.

cards.question: Saul wants to know what's going on. What does he tell the troops with him?

answers.text: Call the roll and see who has left
Sound the horn and gather all Israel
Go and spy on the Philistine camp

cards.text: They call the roll, and two names come up empty: Jonathan and his armor-bearer. Then Saul says to Ahijah the priest, “Bring the ark of God.”
The ark was with the Israelites at that time. But while Saul is still talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp keeps getting louder.

cards.question: With the noise from the Philistine camp growing, what does Saul tell the priest?

cards.text: Then Saul and all his troops gather up and march out to the battle.

cards.question: When Saul's army reaches the Philistines, what do they find?

answers.text: Philistines swinging swords at each other
A Philistine camp left completely empty
Philistines lined up and ready to fight

cards.question: Some Hebrews had gone up into the camps around them to join the Philistines. Now they stay on the Philistine side.
And the Israelites who'd been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim? When they hear the Philistines are fleeing, what do they do?

answers.text: Join the battle and chase them
Stay hidden up in the hills
Head back to their own homes

cards.question: So the ___ saved Israel that day.

cards.text: And the battle moves on beyond Beth-aven. Keep that apron on, friend, because this story's not done yet.

findings.problem: This story card goes back to an earlier line of verse 6 ("Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf") after card 11 has already moved past it. It then restates card 11's answer ("he knows Who can't be stopped"), so it works as a recap and doesn't move the passage forward. The "Perhaps" line belongs on card 10, before the question.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Samuel 14:8. Its second sentence ("Whatever the outpost says next tells them what to do") tells the sign plan from verses 9-10, so the citation is too narrow.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup "Two men started it, but the text says where all that panic came from" rules out the wrong answer Jonathan before the baker picks. Saying "Two men started it" and then "but" points the baker away from Jonathan.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Two men started it" says the two men caused the panic. Verse 15 never says that. It only says panic struck and that the panic spread from God, so the card adds a link between the assault and the panic that the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Nothing on cards 10 or 11 gives the baker a way to reason toward "Withdraw your hand." The cards never set up that Saul has the priest begin something with the ark, so the pick between "Withdraw your hand," "Ask the LORD once more" and "Bring the ark closer" comes down to luck. The baker also leaves without knowing what the line means.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line "this story's not done yet" repeats the doc's example wording ("this story's not done") instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
